edge_explainer: The screen flagged this as a cheap games developer that might be a capitalised-development cash-flow illusion. Primary verification refutes that, and refutes it in the company's favour. Frontier's reported free cash flow already deducts the ~GBP 28.5m of game-development spend (it sits inside the capex line, not below it), and the company's own independently stated cash generation of GBP 18.8m in FY26 - struck after buybacks, leases and development - lands within about GBP 2m of it. Over FY24 and FY25 combined Frontier charged GBP 70.2m of amortisation and impairment against GBP 57.4m capitalised, so capitalisation has been a net headwind to profit over the cycle, not a tailwind; 83% of everything ever capitalised is already written off and the remaining book is only 40% of one year's revenue. Development costs amortise straight-line over one to four years rather than against revenue, which is conservative and is the mechanical reason an ageing back catalogue keeps earning. The annual report has no capital-commitments note at all and minimum guarantees to IP licensors are recognised as a liability when signed (GBP 635k outstanding, down from GBP 3.1m), so the GBP 44m of cash is genuinely unencumbered. There is no defined-benefit pension - the screen's GBP 107k pension proxy is property dilapidations. Meanwhile every estimate line rose through the drawdown: the FY26 profit guide went from ~GBP 11m in January to ~GBP 16m in May to GBP 19.0m delivered, while the shares fell 47% from November to May on no negative announcement. That is a de-rate on rising numbers, and the cost reset behind it is structural - at comparable revenue the company swung from a GBP 28.4m operating loss in FY24 to GBP 19.0m of adjusted operating profit in FY26, with adjusted operating costs down 13%. What holds the score to 6 rather than higher: the business is hit-driven and FY27 leans on one October release, with Planet Coaster 2 as a live cautionary precedent; roughly GBP 10.8m a year of UK creative-industry tax relief - comparable in size to the entire operating profit and flagged by the auditor as an overstatement risk - subsidises the cash generation; the entry is 41.6% off a 91-day-old low and entirely post-news; and the FY26 numbers are an unaudited trading update with the audited detail five weeks away.

screen_corrections.pension: REFUTED as a pension. Screen pension_gross GBP 107k from a long-term-provisions proxy. AR2025 note 20: GBP 100k (FY24 GBP 85k) of property DILAPIDATIONS. AR2025 p.56 confirms defined-contribution only, no DB scheme, no IAS-19 note in 92 pages. DC charge GBP 3.47m FY25. No EV or book-equity adjustment.
screen_corrections.capdev_heavy_flag_dead: SCREEN DEFECT. capex_intangibles is null, so capdev_r is null and capdev_heavy reads false, despite intangible capex of ~GBP 28.5m being ~28% of sales against an 8% threshold. On a games developer this is the single most important flag and it did not fire. Recommend deriving capex_intangibles as capex_total minus capex_ppe when the vendor tag is absent.
screen_corrections.ebit_vs_peak_window: 1.37 is directionally right (not melting) but the four-year window [FY25 8.7 / FY24 -27.0 / FY23 -26.6 / FY22 1.5] truncates FY21, so 'above peak' means above the post-collapse window peak. On the true cycle FY26 is a round trip, not a new high.
screen_corrections.durability_rescue_verdict: DESERVED on this name, but the rule is weakly discriminating. FDEV was one of the 9 rescued by the new cash-generation condition. The rescue is correct here - but 'generated cash on both sides of the EBIT cross' is nearly automatic for a capitalise-and-amortise business, because the loss side is manufactured by amortising and impairing cash spent in prior years (FY24: GBP 28.4m operating loss, +GBP 1.2m net cash movement). The corroboration came from revenue growth, margin and an independent company-stated cash line, not from the rule. Recommend gating the rule to exclude names whose loss year is dominated by amortisation/impairment of previously capitalised spend.
